Closing Date: Type of Position: Faculty - Tenure/Tenure Track Workstudy Position: No Job Type: Regular Work Shift: Sponsorship Available: No Institution Name: University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff is an 1890 Land-Grant HBCU with a diverse student population, competitive degree offerings and stellar faculty. For more than 140 years, the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff has worked to create an environment that inculcates learning, growth and productivity while affording a basic need to its students – a chance to advance. The 15:1 student to teacher ratio makes it possible to maintain a learning environment with close interaction between students and faculty while challenging curricula encourage our students to seek and fulfill their potential. Out-of-class experiences and student involvement include more than 90 student organizations, an internationally renowned Vesper Choir, Marching Band, Concert Bands, Wind Symphony, nationally recognized debate team, award-winning theater department and accomplished athletic program. Though the main campus is in Pine Bluff, its reach is worldwide. UAPB has an extended campus in North Little Rock and offers as well as online courses. With the addition of the Arkansas Research and Education Optical Network (ARE-ON), students can engage in information exchange with others anywhere in the world. There are also Research and Extension offices in Lonoke, Newport and Lake Village and collaborations with other colleges and universities in the State through the National Science Foundation funded STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) Academy. As the second oldest land-grant institution in the state of Arkansas, the mission of this No Excuse University remains the same – to provide a high quality, affordable education with a personal touch. Position Details Position Information Posting Number F0432026 Working Title Assistant Professor of Psychology and Counseling Department Org 347000 - Psychology & Counseling Why should you work at UCA? We are excited that you are considering joining the UCA Family—the faculty, staff, students and alumni—who make the University of Central Arkansas a great place to work!At the University of Central Arkansas, we value our employees striving to maintain a work-life balance. We realize that this affects the overall well-being of employees while learning to prioritize challenging work and the ability to make a difference. Participation in university-wide flexible work schedules may be available for certain positions. Training is provided on systems or job-specific software, and tools are available supporting professional and personal development. The benefits package allows you to customize your benefits to meet your current needs, with the ability to adjust them as your priorities change. This includes university contributions to health, dental, life and disability insurance, 80% tuition waivers for employees and their families, 12 official holidays, immediate leave accrual, and a retirement program with university contributions of 10% of employee salary. Also available are health and wellness incentives, as well as access to sports and cultural activities on campus for the family, free gym membership and equipment rentals. Position Summary The University of Central Arkansas Assistant Professor is responsible for teaching, research and service. This position is governed by state and federal laws and agency/institution policy. The position is tenure track and a nine-month appointment. Job Duties and Responsibilities • Serve as a core member of the undergraduate faculty with some teaching in the graduate programs.• Teach courses in line with program and department needs.• Conduct an active program of research and scholarship with a clearly articulated agenda that supports the involvement of students as research assistants.• Mentor students through academic advising and research.• Serve the department, university, and community in ways that promote psychology. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Areas of scholarship and expertise are open, with some preference in the areas of health psychology, sport psychology, or industrial/organizational psychology. We are eager to support applicants who bring diversity to the department and university. Skills Considered Essential for Success -Knowledge of the organization and administration of higher education.-Knowledge of student development theory.-Knowledge of state, federal, and university rules, regulations, and procedures.-Ability to work in a diverse and dynamic environment.-Ability to compile statistics into reports.-Ability to work collaboratively and independently with common goals as a part of a team.-Ability to make sound judgments and assist in resolving student concerns.-Effective interpersonal communication, writing, and organizational abilities.-Civility in all interactions of a public or confidential nature.-Demonstrate follow-up contacts and consultations in a timely manner. Required Education and/or Experience The formal education of a doctorate in psychology or related field is required. jobs.description: Positions College of Allied Health - CFIT. Seeking qualified applicants for a 10-month principal faculty position for the Harding department of Cardiac Function & Interventional Technology (CFIT); rank will be commensurate with applicant experience. Responsibilities will include working with existing faculty to develop cardiac device continuing education program, teach in the program's core on-ground, and on-line curriculum, advising and mentoring students, assisting with the technology lab, conducting scholarly activity in the faculty's area of expertise, and engaging in service to the college, university, and community. Qualified applicants will be expected to have three plus years’ experience working with cardiac electrophysiology (EP) mapping systems, possess a minimum of a master's degree, a minimum of three years of clinical experience; prior teaching experience and IBHRE certification is preferred. Interested individuals should apply online. Inquiries for additional information may be sent to Kenneth Turley, CFIT director and professor, krturley@harding.edu, or Box 12281, 915 E. Market Ave, Searcy, AR 72149-5615. Posted 7/13/2024 Apply now College of Allied Health - Occupational Therapy Program Director Seeking qualified applicants for a twelve-month position as the Program Director of the Occupational Therapy Program, beginning June 1, 2027. The Program Director of the Occupational Therapy Program serves as the academic and administrative leader of Harding University's Master of Science in Occupational Therapy (MSOT) program, fully accredited by ACOTE. The Program Director is responsible for the management and administration of the program, including strategic planning, curriculum oversight, accreditation, budgeting, assessment, faculty development, continuous program improvement and leadership of the external advisory board. Approximately fifty percent of the position is dedicated to administrative responsibilities, with the remaining responsibilities focused on teaching, scholarship, service and student mentorship as a full-time core faculty member. Successful candidates must have an earned doctoral degree in occupational therapy or related field, must hold current certification by the National Board of Certified Occupational Therapy and must be licensed or eligible for license in Arkansas. A minimum 8 years of experience as an occupational therapist and 4 years full-time experience in an academic appointment is required. Rank will be commensurate with experience. The Harding Occupational Therapy program strongly prioritizes student-centered education, community engagement, and the preparation of competent, ethical occupational therapy practitioners. The successful candidate will join a collaborative faculty committed to academic excellence, Christian service, and the continued growth of the program. Interested individuals should apply online. Inquiries for additional information may be sent to Michael McGalliard, mmcgalliard@harding.edu Box 12287, 915 E. Market Ave, Searcy, AR 72149-5615. jobs.description: Upward Bound College and Career Readiness Lab InstructorJob Summary:The Upward Bound Program is an early intervention pre-college program that helps students prepare for higher education. Upward Bound brings high school students to college campuses after school, on the weekends, and during the summer to receive instruction in core subject areas. The Upward Bound program is seeking applicants for part-time instructor to facilitate a College and Career Readiness Lab for participants in the Federal TRIO Upward Bound Program.Under the direction of the Upward Bound Director, the instructor will guide students through the development of a project based on an interest, talent, skill, problem, or area of curiosity. Students will research, plan, create, test, revise, and present a product, service, performance, portfolio, or demonstration. The instructor will provide coaching, structured feedback, career connections, and support for a culminating Upward Bound Student Showcase. The Upward Bound Instructor is responsible for preparing materials; developing instruction strategies; and evaluating student progress. They are role models, sharing expertise and experiences with participants and maintain required records. Instructors must be able to commit for 18 weeks and work well with staff at all levels within a collaborative environment.Students enter the course with differing academic abilities, interests, skill levels, career goals, learning preferences, and prior project experience. The instructor will create an environment in which students can develop an existing talent or discover and develop a new skill. jobs.description: Welding Technology Instructor ASU Mid-South, a comprehensive community college located just minutes from downtown Memphis, Tennessee, seeks a progressive, student-centered individual to provide instruction in its Welding Technology program to train individuals to fill the growing demand for skilled welding professionals. ASU Mid-South’s Welding Technology program offers students an opportunity to earn four separate certificates of proficiency in four welding processes, a certificate of proficiency in fabrication/fitting, and an Associate of Applied Science Degree that will prepare them to seek rapid entry to employment. This is a full-time, 12-month position with full college benefits. Qualifications: Candidate must hold an associate’s degree in welding technology or related field and at least 5 years of related industry experience. Candidates without an associate’s degree may be considered, but must agree to obtain an appropriate credential within a mutually agreed upon timeframe. Consideration will be given to candidates with greater experience and relevant industry-recognized certifications (i.e. AWS or NCCER certifications). Candidate must have the ability to read/analyze and interpret blueprints and schematics related to the profession. Previous use of Canvas or another Learning Management System (LMS) is a plus. Preference will be given to candidates with prior teaching or industry training experience. A compelling combination of educational background, work experience, and professional credentials may be considered. Other qualifications include excellent interpersonal, written and communication skills; a working knowledge of Microsoft applications; and evidence of ongoing commitment to professional development. Responsibilities: Reports to the Dean for Advanced Manufacturing and Transportation and has responsibility for curriculum, instruction, lab oversight, and industry alignment of the Welding Technology program. Teaching schedule may include evening or weekend hours. Teach courses for the Welding Technology program during the fall, spring, and summer semesters. Deliver instruction to secondary and postsecondary students that aligns with approved ASU Mid-South syllabi and academic standards, supporting student attainment of course- and program-level learning outcomes. Develop and provide non-credit, customized training for employer partners. Build positive relationships with vendors and local manufacturing employers in eastern Arkansas and the Greater Memphis region in support of employer training needs and to foster engagement in program initiatives and the Welding Technology Advisory Council. Support development of curriculum in response to Advisory Council input and ensure program alignment with industry-recognized certifications and local industry needs. Monitor emerging industry trends and technologies to ensure relevance of Welding Technology curriculum and training aids. Maintain accurate attendance and grade records using the College’s Learning Management System. Collaborate with relevant grant-sponsored programs to attain grant objectives and support the College’s track record of success with executing federal, state, and privately-funded grant-sponsored initiatives. Help maintain equipment and supplies inventory and determine ongoing programmatic and instructional equipment and supply needs. Ensure lab areas are clean, well-maintained, and compliant with appropriate safety standards. Participate in institutional and programmatic student recruitment and retention initiatives; help to identify methods and markets related to Welding Technology student recruitment. Serve as an academic program advisor for students enrolled in the Welding Technology program. Participate in SkillsUSA activities and events. Understand and comply with College policies and procedures. Participate in registration, commencement, and other required activities. Serve on College committees, including program advisory committees. Salary:

Department: COSMOS - Provisional Positions Department's Website: https://cosmos.ualr.edu/ Summary of Job Duties: The Postdoctoral Fellow position is a full-time, provisional position with the COSMOS Research Center (cosmos.ualr.edu) at the University of Arkansas and is funded through a grant or contract. The position renewal is contingent upon continued grant funding and satisfactory job performance. The Postdoctoral Fellow will develop socio-computational models to advance our understanding of cyber campaigns on social media, grounded in the dynamics of social and communication processes such as group formation, activation, decentralized decision-making, and collective action. The Postdoctoral Fellow will help extract relevant open-source information in a guided snowball data collection manner by leveraging cyber forensics and deep web search-based methodologies. Postdoctoral Fellow will work with the research team in developing predictive models of various socio-technical behaviors on different social media platforms (including multimedia-rich platforms), and usable tools/software to identify key actors and key groups responsible for coordinating cyber campaigns and disseminating propaganda. This is an on-campus position. This position is governed by state and federal laws, and agency/institution policy. The position reports to Prof. Nitin Agarwal (nxagarwal@ualr.edu), Maulden-Entergy Endowed Chair & Donaghey Distinguished Professor, and Director, COSMOS Research Center at UA-Little Rock. Department: Instruction Department's Website: Summary of Job Duties: Responsibilities: Primary duties include serving as the EMS Program Director and Lead Instructor. This includes coordinating and supervising all EMS program courses to ensure compliance with CoAEMSP accreditation and ARDEMS regulations. The instructor will teach EMS, NAEMT, and AHA classes and coordinate all EMS and AHA continuing education courses. Additional responsibilities include maintaining clinical affiliate agreements, coordinating with the Advisory Committee, and preparing regulatory reports. The position requires a willingness to learn online teaching requirements, teach evening classes, serve on university committees, and perform other duties assigned by the Assistant Vice Chancellor and the Director of Allied Health. Qualifications: Qualifications: Must have a bachelor's degree or equivalent (preferably in EMS, health/health related field, or education), be an Arkansas Certified Paramedic Instructor, and be a Nationally Registered Paramedic. Must possess a current, unencumbered paramedic license with a minimum of 2 years' experience; 3-5 years preferred. Documented education or experience in instructional methodology is required. Experience with National Registry Standards and accreditation processes is preferred. Additional Information: Salary: Commensurate with qualifications and experience/Excellent fringe benefits.
